title: Extreme heat
summary: Above 90°F for 2 to 3 days. Fans don't cool you above 95°F. Know heat stroke (above 103°F) and when to call 911.

sources.title: WTVR: Henrico County heat wave, cooling centers (July 3, 2026)

blocks.text: **Extreme heat** in Virginia means temperatures above **90°F for 2 to 3 days or more**, with humidity. Older adults, children, and people who are sick or overweight are at higher risk.

items: Find out where you can cool off: libraries, malls, community centers. Henrico has opened cooling centers during heat waves (July 2026: Libbie Mill Library and Eastern Henrico Recreation Center). A Salvation Army cooling shelter on Chamberlayne Avenue opens when temperatures are 92°F or higher. Call Henrico Emergency Management at (804) 501-5162 or dial 2-1-1 to check.
Block heat: close drapes, weather-strip doors and windows, add insulation.
No air conditioning? **Go to a cooling center.**
**Don't rely on a fan.** Fans don't lower body temperature. Don't use them as your main cooling when it's above 95°F outside.
Take cool showers or baths. Drink plenty of fluids. Wear loose, light-colored clothing.
Limit oven use. Avoid hard work in midday heat. Seek shade and wear a wide-brimmed hat.
**Never leave people or pets in a closed car.**
Check on older adults, neighbors and family.
Pets: shade, plenty of cool water. Hot pavement burns paws.

rows: Muscle pain or spasms in stomach, arms or legs
Move to a cooler place, loosen clothing, sip cool sports drinks. Get medical help if cramps last over 1 hour.
Heavy sweating, pale skin, cramps, tiredness, weakness, dizziness, headache, nausea or vomiting, fainting
Go to a cool or air-conditioned place and lie down, loosen clothing, cool bath, sip sports drinks. Get medical help if it worsens or lasts over **1 hour**.
Oral temperature above **103°F**, red hot dry skin with **no sweat**, fast strong pulse, dizziness, confusion, unconsciousness
**Call 911** or get to a hospital now. Move to shade. Cool the person any way you can: cold wet cloths or ice packs on the head, neck, armpits and groin.

blocks.text: Heat stroke is an emergency. Call 911.
Heat is also a risk for insulin. See the T1D insulin storage guide.
